$comment: GENERATED by scripts/compose-schema.py from profiles/ — edit the overlays, not this file. The BASE every brain composes. Carries the ontology envelope (version, contract, classes), the kinds every scope has regardless of purpose (documents, memory, terms, sessions, decisions, questions, extracted entities, activity), the general edge vocabulary, and the identity/taxonomy edges federation depends on (same_as, facet_of, aligns_with, asserted_by, supersedes, contradicts, tagged_with, broader — promoted from the company brain where they were first designed). scripts/compose-schema.py merges this with the overlays declared in client.config.json (profile.base + profile.overlays) into brain-schema.json, which every consumer keeps reading unchanged.

contract.$comment: The supergraph interop contract (#60): the global address grammar, per-kind id conventions, realm definitions, and join-edge set that let every graph in the system (compiled brain, extracted KG, doc link graph, live code graph, federated subrepo brains) address and traverse one another as ONE NETWORK. Producers declare which contract version they emit and conform at their OUTPUT boundary — integrate, don't refactor: internal ids stay whatever they are; a thin mapping/export layer produces conformant addresses. The grammar codifies the id shape the brain already uses (kind:slug), so existing artifacts are conformant as-is. Version bumps ride the migrate-brain discipline.

address.notes: repo is the federation namespace, applied by aggregate-brains when a node brain federates upward; instance-local addresses omit it. kind is a declared kind id from this file. id follows the kind's convention below. Code-realm addresses are owned by the code realm (repo-relative path + qualified symbol) and appear only as join-edge targets.

path.rule: repo-relative POSIX path (the file IS the identity)

slug.rule: kebab-case slug, unique within the kind

external.rule: the external tracker's native key, verbatim

brain.authority: the instance repo; source of truth for every kind declared in this file

code.store: live code-graph database, rebuilt from source
code.traversal: join edges continue via the code-graph query surface; code nodes are never compiled into the brain

kinds.title: Document
kinds.description: Authored knowledge-base markdown; indexed into the pack, rendered by the reader, linked via [[wikilinks]] and relative links (#49).

kinds.title: Wiki Page
kinds.description: Committed mirror of the GitHub wiki (make wiki-sync); edited at the wiki, never in place.

kinds.title: Memory Note
kinds.description: Authored engagement memory compiled as Memory nodes. Tracker records remain in their declared JSON authorities; frontmatter migration requires an explicit adapter.

kinds.title: Glossary Term
kinds.description: Shared vocabulary. Fill-in twin of memory/glossary.md until #51 lands.

kinds.title: Session
kinds.description: A meeting/recording and its analyses (PlanOpticon pipeline). A record of what happened: append-only, never retuned.

kinds.title: Decision
kinds.description: A decision trace: what was decided, when, by whom, superseded-by. The procedural layer's spine.

kinds.title: Open Question
kinds.description: An unresolved question routed to its owner. The upward escalation channel for blocked work (#55).

kinds.title: KG Entity
kinds.description: An extracted semantic-layer entity (concept, technology, organization, person, term). Provenance and edge vocabulary per #57.

kinds.title: Activity Event
kinds.description: An activity event derived from a producer log; retention and refresh policy belong to its source. The default homepage feed is a rolling Git projection.

kinds.title: Organization
kinds.description: A register entry for an organization (client, partner, vendor, the owner itself): the scope-level entity table that lets two brains name the same company without merging their data. Stakeholders affiliate to it; equivalences across brains resolve to it. Authored and reviewed, never extracted.

kinds.title: Person
kinds.description: A register entry for a person, bound to one principal (OIDC issuer + subject) that every host trusts: the scope-level entity table that lets two brains name the same person without merging their data. Access emails and consumer credentials resolve to the principal at the host boundary; equivalences across brains resolve to the node. Authored and reviewed, never extracted.

kinds.title: RAID Item
kinds.description: Risk / assumption / issue / dependency register entry; escalation channel alongside open questions.

kinds.title: Stakeholder
kinds.description: A person or group with a role in the engagement; owns decisions, questions, and work.

kinds.title: Issue
kinds.description: Committed snapshot of the external issue tracker (make issues); history in app/issues-history.json.

kinds.title: Dependency
kinds.description: Dependency edges across the plan, derived from the specs tree; the work graph's edge list.

kinds.title: Action Item
kinds.description: Executable follow-up extracted from sessions; the smallest dispatchable unit besides a story.

kinds.title: User Story
kinds.description: A story with acceptance criteria; work-class and dispatchable under #55.

kinds.title: Spec Node
kinds.description: A node of the plan tree (phase > epic > feature > story). The work graph's node set; stories are the dispatch unit.

kinds.title: Deliverable
kinds.description: A committed output with status; closing work nodes moves deliverables.

kinds.title: Roadmap Item
kinds.description: Strategy-cadence work. Owned by the slow loop: fast-tier agents escalate to it, never edit it (#55).

kinds.title: Data Source
kinds.description: A system of record in the data-source inventory (#13): a database, warehouse, API, or file drop the engagement reads from.

kinds.title: Source Entity
kinds.description: A table/collection within a Source. Structural truth about the shape of the data, regenerated from the source itself.

kinds.title: Source Field
kinds.description: A column/attribute within a source Entity. The leaf of the data-source inventory.

kinds.title: Governed Metric
kinds.description: A reviewed, source-bound measure projected from the structured authority.

kinds.title: Catalog
kinds.description: A manifest node standing for a named collection of artifacts, so the set itself is addressable and not merely implied by its members.

kinds.title: Analysis Artifact
kinds.description: A standalone analysis output listed in the artifacts catalog.

kinds.title: Collection
kinds.description: A named set of nodes, of any kinds, addressable as one thing. Members join via member_of. The primitive behind a training split, a review queue, or a release scope — a slice you want to name and query, not re-derive from a filter each time.

edges.description: Hierarchy: phase contains epic contains feature contains story; group contains member.
A record or work node is about a knowledge node (decision about a concept).
A decision trace anchors to the session it was decided in.
Doc-to-doc link ([[wikilink]] or relative markdown link); indexed as backlinks (#49).
General semantic association between entities; the weakest edge, prefer a stronger verb.
Canonical extraction verb: source consumes or operates target. Free verbs canonicalize onto this set (#57).
Canonical extraction verb: source supplies data or capability to target (#57).
Canonical extraction verb: bidirectional system integration (#57).
A stakeholder owns a decision, question, deliverable, or work node.
Reserved (#55): a fast-tier signal (open question, RAID item) raised against a slow-tier target.
Join edge (#60): a work or record node is realized by a code-realm target (repo, module, symbol). Target addresses are realm-qualified; traversal continues in the code graph.
Federation anchor: a namespaced node belongs to a product-node repo (aggregate-brains).

Replacement: this node takes the place of that one. A change of direction is NEVER an edit; it is a new node with a supersedes edge, so the prior decision stays readable and the path to the current position is a graph walk. Resolution, not open disagreement.

Unresolved disagreement: these two nodes cannot both be right and nobody has decided which wins. Distinct from supersedes on purpose, so the brain can hold a live contradiction without pretending it is settled.

Controlled-vocabulary labelling: a node is tagged with a glossary term. Preferred over the free-form `labels` string list, because a term node carries a definition, synonyms and a place in the taxonomy, which a bare string cannot.

Taxonomy (SKOS-style): the target is a broader concept than the source. Distinct from `contains`, which is part-of composition; this is is-a. Traverse it inbound for narrower terms rather than declaring a second inverse relation.

Strict identity: these two nodes are the SAME entity under different ids, and a consumer may treat them as one. Reserve it for that. Two brains describing a subject differently are not the same node — use facet_of. Federation cannot dedup without this, but over-applying it destroys the per-brain resolution that made the brains worth federating.

A perspective on a shared subject. Sales and engineering legitimately resolve the same topic at different granularity and with different concerns; both are authoritative in their own brain. The facet keeps its own identity, data and owner, and points at the concept it is a view OF — so the two are linked and comparable without either being flattened into the other.

Cross-brain correspondence weaker than identity: these two nodes are about the same thing, and nobody has decided whether they are one entity, two facets, or merely adjacent. The honest edge to emit when a linker finds a strong match it cannot justify promoting to same_as or facet_of.
Attribution as an edge, for when the asserter is itself a node (a person, an agent, a generator). Complements the asserted_by PROPERTY, which carries a bare identity string when no such node exists.

Membership in an organization: a person (stakeholder) is affiliated with an Organization register entry. Populated from stakeholder.org when a matching organization exists; a name matching no register entry emits nothing.
A question or action was raised in a recorded session.
Unclassified extraction relation; original verb remains in source evidence. No stronger meaning is implied.
Work-graph ordering: source cannot complete before target.
A work node's provenance to the decision or open question it cites (a story's references: frontmatter -> gen-brain.py's record_links linker, #55).
A work node has this immediate parent in the plan DAG.
Readiness evidence that this work node is blocked by another work node.
Consecutive work nodes on the computed critical dependency path.
Set membership: the source node belongs to a named Collection. Lets an arbitrary slice across kinds be addressed as one thing — a training split, a review queue, a release scope.
A catalogued source exposes a structured entity.
A structured entity contains a declared field.
A governed metric reads from its declared system of record.
A governed metric measures a declared source entity.
The metric aggregates this declared source field.
A declared field by which a metric may be grouped.
The metric's declared temporal grain field.
A declared field by which a metric may be filtered.
A business term defines a governed metric.
A business term governs a source entity or field.
An analysis artifact is registered in this catalog.

contextRecipes.$comment: Agent dispatch (#55 slice 1): a declared graph traversal that assembles a work node's task pack — context assembly is a traversal, not a grep. Keyed by the compiled brain node's `kind` field (Story, ActionItem, ...); `default` covers any kind with no override. scripts/gen-task-pack.py walks each hop's rel/direction from the task node (or transitively, repeating the hop until nothing new resolves) and assembles the result under the hop's `as` key.

taxonomy.label: Context information
taxonomy.definition: Categories of knowledge needed for a named context use case.

taxonomy.label: Identity and boundaries
taxonomy.definition: Subject, mandate, terminology, inclusions and exclusions.

taxonomy.label: Purpose and outcomes
taxonomy.definition: Problem, beneficiaries, desired outcomes and measures.

taxonomy.label: Actors and accountability
taxonomy.definition: People, organizations, roles and decision authority.

taxonomy.label: Operating context
taxonomy.definition: Systems, capabilities, processes, resources and dependencies.

taxonomy.label: Constraints and commitments
taxonomy.definition: Requirements, policies, obligations and acceptance criteria.

taxonomy.label: Evidence and observations
taxonomy.definition: Sources, measurements and exact supporting fragments.

taxonomy.label: Decisions and rationale
taxonomy.definition: Chosen options, alternatives, authority and effective dates.

taxonomy.label: Work and change
taxonomy.definition: Actions, ownership, dependencies and actual outcomes.
